teaching.hint: Which interval leaves the most room for later compatible choices?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Minimizing removals is maximizing kept intervals; an earliest finishing interval can be exchanged into an optimal compatible selection.
solution_outline.approach: Order intervals by ending coordinate and keep each interval whose start is at least the end of the last kept interval. Subtract the number kept from the input count.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The kept set is compatible, and its last end is the earliest possible finishing boundary after that many greedy choices.
solution_outline.correctness: Replace the first interval of any optimal set by the earliest finishing interval without harming later compatibility; repeat on the remaining candidates. Thus the greedy kept count is maximal.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n log n)` time for sorting and `O(1)` auxiliary scan state beyond sorting storage.
solution_outline.pitfall: Treating endpoint equality as overlap rejects compatible intervals.
